question: When ordinary people sing a favourite pop record from memory, how close do they get to its original key?
answer: Often remarkably close. Daniel Levitin asked people without musical training to sing the opening of songs they knew from recordings; many hit the original pitch or came within a semitone or two, though none could name a single note. Remembering pitch is common. What is rare is having a label for it.
move: A skill can be widespread when only the naming of it is rare.
ask: What do I already do well without ever having had a name for it?
reference: Levitin, Absolute memory for musical pitch: evidence from the production of learned melodies, Perception & Psychophysics, 1994
